title: Feat: Workflows now AI executable, updated slash_command tool allows agentic autonomous discovery & execution
author: James-Cherished

test_results.note: Comprehensive unit tests present in PR, but no integration testing evidence

key_findings: Breaking change: Experiment rename (runSlashCommand → autoExecuteWorkflow) without migration path
Scope explosion: 54 files combining 3-4 distinct PRs (workflow discovery, tool migration, UI fixes, i18n updates)
Unrelated changes: Husky pre-push hook modifications (memory limits, timeouts) don't belong in this PR
Unrelated changes: .gitignore adds Python venv patterns in a TypeScript project
Changeset confusion: 6 changesets with conflicting semver (1 minor, 5 patch)
Excellent architecture: Workflow discovery service is well-designed with caching, symlink support, graceful error handling
Comprehensive tests: 226-line metadata extractor tests with edge cases, updated tool tests
Incomplete i18n: Only English translation fully updated, 15 other locales use old terminology
blocking_issues: Breaking change breaks existing user configs without migration
PR combines too many independent changes - should be split into 3-4 PRs
Infrastructure changes (husky hooks) lack justification and belong in separate PR
.gitignore changes (env/, venv/) unexplained in TypeScript project
lessons: Scope creep indicators: Multiple changesets, unrelated file types, breaking changes mixed with bug fixes
Configuration changes need justification: Why 3072MB memory? Why 300s timeout? What problem does this solve?
Experiment migrations need first-class support: Add migration map and auto-migrate old keys to new keys
i18n workflow improvement: Either update all locales or mark non-English as needing translation
Terminology consistency matters: 'slash commands' vs 'workflows' creates confusion across codebase
Well-designed architecture undermined by poor PR hygiene: Excellent code quality but review complexity makes merge risky
review_methodology: Comprehensive analysis of 54 files: Read all 6 changesets, analyzed architecture patterns, identified scope issues within first 100 lines, verified test coverage, documented breaking changes and unrelated modifications
